newsitem.title: FRANCE: France would reject GEC bid on Thomson - paper.
newsitem.headline: France would reject GEC bid on Thomson - paper.

text.p: The French government will not accept Britain's GEC Plc as a candidate for the privatisation of defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF, the newspaper Le Figaro said on Friday.

It said the government was expected to accept only Lagardere Groupe and Alcatel Alsthom as candidates to acquire its 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF, which is part of the Thomson group, when it announces which suitors are qualified to bid next Monday.
The newpaper named no source for its report.

"GEC will not be authorised to compete to take over Thomson-CSF. The British company, in accordance with the procedure set out by the government, has offered its candidacy. But the matter will stop there, with the government declining to authorise GEC to go further," the newspaper said.

It said the government might or might not elucidate the reasons for its decision. The government has said it is open to European offers but has noted that the privatisation involves national security.

Under the privatisation timetable, the government must decide by April 7 which candidacies it accepts. The candidates must submit final offers by May 7 and the government expects to announce its choice before the end of June.
Alcatel and Lagardere have said they are candidates.
